<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par44 />Aramaic), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אָֽזְלַת|translate=it is gone}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=36}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְנִשְׁכַּ֫חַת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=15}} (in the Aramaic form, for {{GHGheb|text=וְנִשְׁכְּחָה}}); from a verb {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְשָׁבַת}}, cf. {{GHGpar|72|o}}. This original feminine ending ''-ath'' is regularly retained before suffixes, see {{GHGpar|59|a}}; and similarly in stems {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, either in the form ''āth'' (which is frequent also in stems {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}} {{GHGpar|74|g}}), or with the {{GHGterm|Pathaḥ}} weakened to {{GHGterm|vocal Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} before the pleonastic ending {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=גָּֽלְתָה}} {{GHGpar|75|i}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=31|verse=5}} the Aramaic form {{GHGheb|text=גָּֽבְהָא}} occurs instead of {{GHGheb|text=גָּֽבְהָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|44|g}}
2nd {{GHGterm|masc.}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּה}} for {{GHGheb|text=תָּ}} (differing only orthographically), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בָּגַ֫דְתָּה|translate=thou hast dealt treacherously}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal|chapter=2|verse=14}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=12}} ({{GHGheb|text=נָתַ֫תָּה}} which is twice as common as {{GHGheb|text=נָתַ֫תָּ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|66|h}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=56|verse=9}} (so also in ''Hiphʿil''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=60|verse=4}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|44|h}}
2nd {{GHGterm|fem.}} has sometimes a Yodh at the end, as in {{GHGheb|text=הָלָ֑כְתְּי|translate=thou wentest}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=21}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=33|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=4.5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=19|hidebook=1}} (but read the ptcp. {{GHGheb|text=שֹׁמַ֫עַת}}, with the LXX, instead of the 2nd fem.),{{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=46|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, and so commonly in Jeremiah, and Ez ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, &c.); see also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=3|verse=3.4}}. {{GHGheb|text=הָלַ֫כְתִּי}}, &c., is really intended, for the vowel signs in the text belong to the marginal reading {{GHGheb|text=הָלַכְתְּ}} (without {{GHGheb|text=י}})<ref>Where the Masora apparently regards the {{GHGheb|text=תִּי}} as the termination of the 2nd ''sing. fem.'', e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=20}} (twice), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=13}}, it has rather taken the form as 1st ''pers. sing.'' (cf. Stade, ''Gramm.'', p. 253); so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=7}}, where {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫מְתִּי}}, on account of verse 12, must either have originally been intended as 2nd ''sing. fem.'', or is due to an erroneous pronunciation of the form {{GHGheb|text=קמת}} as {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫מְתִּ}} instead of 3rd ''sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מַת}} (as LXX).</ref> as in the corresponding pronoun {{GHGheb|text=אַתְּי}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַתִּי}}) {{GHGpar|32|h}}. The ordinary form has rejected the final ''i'', but it regularly reappears when pronominal suffixes are added ({{GHGpar|59|a}}, c).

{{GHGmargin-letter|44|i}}
1st ''pers. comm.'' sometimes without Yodh, as {{GHGheb|text=יָדַ֫עְתִּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=140|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=48}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=59}} (all in K<sup>e</sup>thîbh), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=16|verse=2}}, without a Q<sup>e</sup>rê; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=18|verse=20}} also {{GHGheb|text=אָמַ֫רְתִּ}} is really intended, as appears from {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=5}}. The Q<sup>e</sup>rê requires the ordinary form, to which the vowels of the text properly belong, whilst the K<sup>e</sup>thîbh is probably to be regarded as the remains of an earlier orthography, which omitted vowel-letters even at the end of the word.

{{GHGmargin-letter|44|k}}
{{GHGheb|text=תֶן}} as the termination of the 2nd ''plur. m.'' for {{GHGheb|text=תֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=26}}, might just possibly be due to the following {{GHGheb|text=ת}} (cf., for an analogous case, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=3|verse=12}}, {{GHGpar|87|e}}), but is probably a copyist’s error. Plur. 2nd {{GHGterm|fem.}} in {{GHGheb|text=-תֶּ֫נָה}} (according to others {{GHGheb|text=-תֶּ֫נָּה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=4|verse=3}}, but the reading is very doubtful; since {{GHGheb|text=ה}} follows, it is perhaps merely due to dittography; cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=אַתֵּ֫נָה}} {{GHGpar|32|i}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|44|l}}
3rd ''plur. comm.'' has three times the very strange termination {{GHGheb|text=וּן}}<ref>That these examples can hardly be referred to a primitive Semitic ending ''ûn'' in the 3rd plur. Perf., has been shown by Nöldeke in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} vol. 38, p. 409 ff.; cf. also {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} vol. 32, p. 757 f., where G. Hoffmann proves that the terminations in ''Nûn'' of the 3rd plur. in Aramaic, formerly adduced by us, are secondary forms. [See also Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Heb. Tenses}}<sup>3</sup>, p. 6 ''note''.]</ref>; {{GHGheb|text=יָֽדְעוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=3.16}} (both before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, and hence, no doubt, if the text is correct, to avoid a hiatus), and in the still more doubtful form {{GHGheb|text=צָקוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=16}}; on {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} in the Imperf. see {{GHGpar|47|m}}; on the affixed {{GHGheb|text=א}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=10|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=12}}, see {{GHGpar|23|i}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|44|m}}
It is very doubtful whether, as in most Semitic languages (see {{GHGpar|47|c}}, note), the 3rd.''fem. plur.'' in Hebrew was originally distinguished from the 3rd ''masc''.<section end=par44 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
